hook: A standardized checklist-based log of approximately 100 UFO incident summaries collected by the U.S. Army Air Forces between July 1947 and January 1948, beginning with a cluster of disc and sphere sightings at Muroc Army Air Field (later Edwards AFB) by multiple military officers, test pilots, and civilian staff.
why_it_matters: This document captures the earliest formal military UFO investigation records, made contemporaneously during the weeks immediately following the June 1947 Kenneth Arnold sighting that catalyzed public awareness. Several Muroc incidents carry the explicit evaluation 'Confirmed by other sources,' indicating cross-corroboration rather than isolated anecdotes—and the witnesses include active test pilots operating experimental aircraft. The inclusion of Incident #99 and #100 from Finland, sourced through the U.S. Military Attaché in Helsinki, demonstrates that Army intelligence was aggregating international reports into the same standardized tracking system from the very start.

key_findings.finding: Multiple military witnesses at Muroc AAF on July 8, 1947 independently observed two silver disc-like or spherical objects traveling at approximately 300 MPH at 8,000 ft heading north, followed by a third object performing tight circles the witnesses stated exceeded any known aircraft capability. The official evaluation explicitly reads 'Confirmed by other sources.'

key_findings.finding: Major J.C. Wise, a test pilot at Muroc, observed a yellowish-white sphere 5 to 10 feet in diameter at 10,000–12,000 feet altitude on July 7, 1947, oscillating in a forward whirling movement without losing altitude while traveling 200–225 MPH west to east. The sighting occurred while he was running up the XP-84 experimental aircraft on the ground.

The object was yellowish white in color and I would estimate that it was a sphere about 5 to 10 feet in diameter.

key_findings.finding: A female witness at Muroc independently corroborated the disc sightings, ruling out weather balloons and birds on separate grounds: the objects flew horizontally (not with wind drift) and reflected sunlight. She also judged the circling object's radius impossible for any familiar aircraft type.

key_findings.finding: Incident #98 (November 2, 1947, Houston, Texas) describes a large spinning fireball approximately 26–30 inches in diameter with a 20-foot tail that fell toward a residential field and suddenly extinguished just before reaching the ground. The witness described it as 'almost round, maybe a little oval or saucer-shaped.'

key_findings.finding: Incidents #99 and #100, sourced from the U.S. Military Attaché in Helsinki, document two Finnish sightings in January 1948: a shining object with a long tail near Vaasa (west-to-east, 30 seconds) and a shining object near Pietarsaari that ejected flames and left grey streaks in the sky (north-to-south, 10 seconds), showing the Army was globally aggregating UAP reports through diplomatic intelligence channels.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: These standardized 'Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects' forms are the direct precursor records that fed into Project Sign and then Project Blue Book, representing the Army Air Forces' earliest systematic UFO data collection effort.

Wright-Patterson AFB was the administrative home of Project Sign/Blue Book and the Air Materiel Command's technical analysis arm; these Muroc incident reports would have been routed there for evaluation.

Incidents #99 and #100 were sourced through the U.S. Military Attaché in Helsinki, demonstrating early allied intelligence sharing of UAP reports from Scandinavia into the U.S. military tracking system.

Multiple incidents occurred at Muroc Army Air Field (later Edwards AFB / Groom Lake test range complex), the same desert lake-bed region associated with subsequent classified aircraft testing and UAP sightings.
